title: Xanthe and the Cipher
premise: Estate lawyer Wendell Ashgrove is summoned to read the will of Marguerite Voss, a recluse officially declared dead seven years ago—yet the will is dated three days ago. Among her effects he finds two letters: one confessing to a drowning no body ever explained, and one promising 'the rest' to whoever finds the witness everyone swears is dead. As Wendell traces the cipher hidden in the will's clauses, he realizes Marguerite faked her death to escape a family that killed once before, and that the 'witness' is her own daughter, raised under another name. In the climax, Wendell exposes the family's old crime at the tide-flats where the body was taken, choosing justice outside the law over the bar's silence; the daughter inherits everything, and Wendell finally abandons his own carefully invisible life.
about_author: Felix Quintana is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent a decade watching families unravel over paper. He writes mysteries about the quiet crimes hidden inside legal documents, and lives within earshot of the sea.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Wendell Ashgrove receives a courier packet: a will for Marguerite Voss, dated last week, though she's been dead seven years. His firm's partners urge him to decline. Wendell, a man who has built a career on being unnoticed, accepts instead. POV: Wendell. Beat: uneasy curiosity overriding professional caution.

chapters.title: Two Letters, One Envelope
chapters.summary: At the Voss estate, a solicitor hands Wendell twin letters found in Marguerite's desk—one confessing to a drowning at Greyhaven Tide-Flats, one promising 'the rest' to whoever solves her cipher. The will's clauses are written in deliberate riddles. POV: Wendell. Beat: the moment mystery becomes obligation.

chapters.title: A Death Already Filed
chapters.summary: Wendell pulls the 2017 death certificate and coroner's report: body never recovered, presumed lost at sea. Yet the confession letter describes the drowning in intimate detail. He begins a private index of contradictions. POV: Wendell. Beat: the lawyer's instinct for paperwork as a weapon.

chapters.title: The House That Remembers
chapters.summary: Wendell returns to the shuttered Voss house and finds it recently lived in: fresh flowers, a warm kettle, a child's drawing dated last month. Someone has been maintaining the fiction of death. POV: Wendell. Beat: dread dressed as domesticity.

chapters.title: The Nephew Who Waits
chapters.summary: Silas Voss, Marguerite's heir by the old will, confronts Wendell at the firm, all charm and threat, urging him to honor the 2017 documents. Wendell notices Silas's cufflinks match a description in the confession letter. POV: Wendell. Beat: first open antagonism.

chapters.title: Cipher in the Clauses
chapters.summary: Late-night work: the will's odd bequests—'to the lighthouse that no longer turns,' 'to the year the tide was wrong'—form an acrostic pointing to Greyhaven Tide-Flats and a date: the night before Marguerite's official death. POV: Wendell. Beat: intellectual thrill, the puzzle yielding.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Records Office
chapters.summary: A records clerk named Ivy Corrigan quietly slips Wendell a sealed box Marguerite left 'for the lawyer who asks twice.' Inside: photographs of the Voss family and one of a young girl, labeled 'E.' Ivy warns him to stop. POV: Wendell. Beat: an unexpected ally with her own fear.

chapters.title: What the Tide Took
chapters.summary: Wendell walks the tide-flats at low water, reconstructing the confession letter against the landscape. He finds a rusted strongbox half-buried, empty except for a child's bracelet engraved 'E.' POV: Wendell. Beat: the past made physical, grief without a name yet.

chapters.title: The Confession, Reread
chapters.summary: Interleaved chapter: Marguerite's confession letter in full, revealing she witnessed her brother drown a business partner in 2017 and helped hide the body, then staged her own disappearance to protect the dead man's daughter. POV: Marguerite (letter). Beat: the moral center of the book, sympathy for a liar.

chapters.title: Silas Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Silas invites Wendell to dinner and offers him a partnership and a quiet settlement to certify the old will. Wendell declines with lawyerly politeness and knows he's now a target. That night his office is searched. POV: Wendell. Beat: the cost of refusal becomes real.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: Wendell interviews the family doctor, the harbor master, and the housekeeper—each swears they saw Marguerite's body or signed her death papers. Their stories are identical, word for word. Rehearsed. POV: Wendell. Beat: the wall of complicity; isolation deepens.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse That No Longer Turns
chapters.summary: Following a cipher clause, Wendell explores the derelict Greyhaven lighthouse and finds Marguerite's living quarters—journals, cash, and a second cipher key. Footsteps above; someone flees. POV: Wendell. Beat: hope and danger arriving together.

chapters.title: Ivy's Secret
chapters.summary: Ivy Corrigan admits she is the dead partner's sister and has been leaving supplies for Marguerite for years. She believes Marguerite is still alive and hiding nearby. Wendell realizes the 'witness' may be someone else entirely. POV: Wendell. Beat: alliance cemented; the question reframed.

chapters.title: The Year the Tide Was Wrong
chapters.summary: Decoding the final clause, Wendell learns the drowning happened on a night the tide tables were altered—someone with harbor access moved the body. Only three people could have done it. POV: Wendell. Beat: the net tightening around the living, not the dead.

chapters.title: Silas's Version
chapters.summary: Silas, cornered, tells his own story: Marguerite was unstable, the confession a fantasy. But he slips one true detail—the girl 'E' was sent abroad and 'didn't take.' Wendell understands the girl was meant to die too. POV: Wendell. Beat: cold fury beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: The Drawing of a Door
chapters.summary: Matching the child's drawing from the house to the estate's floor plans, Wendell finds a sealed servant's door behind the library shelving. Behind it: a stair, a lamp still warm, and a note in a child's hand: 'She said to wait for the lawyer.' POV: Wendell. Beat: breath-held discovery.

chapters.title: Elena
chapters.summary: Wendell meets Elena, now nineteen, raised in hiding by Marguerite—alive, and the sole witness to the 2017 drowning as a child. She has the 'rest' of the letters and the altered tide charts. She trusts no one, least of all lawyers. POV: Elena. Beat: the witness found; guarded, fierce, grieving.

chapters.title: The Trap at the Flats
chapters.summary: Silas, tipped off by a firm mole, comes for Elena at the tide-flats at night. Wendell and Ivy intervene; a struggle in the rising water nearly takes Wendell. Ivy records Silas's threats. POV: Wendell. Beat: physical climax, fear and resolve fused.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Rather than trust the firm or the police Silas may have bought, Wendell convenes the witnesses—doctor, harbor master, housekeeper, Ivy, Elena—and plays the confession and recording. The rehearsed wall breaks; the truth is spoken aloud, on the record, before the tide. POV: Wendell. Beat: the book's moral climax; law subordinated to truth.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Wendell formally reads the true will: everything to Elena, with Marguerite's letter read aloud—her confession, her love, her request that the girl live visible and unafraid. Silas is arrested on the recording. POV: Wendell. Beat: ceremony as catharsis; inheritance restored to its rightful meaning.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Grave
chapters.summary: Elena chooses to bury the empty coffin properly, and Marguerite, found living quietly in the lighthouse's sister station, watches from the cliff, choosing to remain 'dead' but present. Elena lets her. POV: Elena. Beat: bittersweet mercy; identity as a chosen thing.

chapters.title: The Man Who Stopped Being Invisible
chapters.summary: Wendell resigns from the firm, takes Elena on as executor of his own newly written will, and opens a small practice 'for the paperwork of the disappeared.' The final image: the tide giving up nothing more, because everything it took has been returned. POV: Wendell. Beat: quiet resolution; the invisible man made visible by doing right.
